# Postgres to Apache Doris

Since version 4.1, [Apache Doris](https://doris.apache.org/), a columnar analytical database that
speaks the MySQL protocol, can follow Postgres by itself, with no Kafka or Debezium to deploy. One
statement creates the target tables, copies the existing rows and streams changes from a
replication slot. In the lab, changes took 5 to 11 seconds to arrive, schema changes came across on
their own, and a `vector` column arrived as NULL without an error. This is the statement the lab ran:

```sql
CREATE JOB pg_mirror_job
PROPERTIES ("max_interval" = "1")
ON STREAMING
FROM POSTGRES (
    "jdbc_url" = "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/app",
    "driver_url" = "https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.4/postgresql-42.7.4.jar",
    "driver_class" = "org.postgresql.Driver",
    "user" = "app", "password" = "...",
    "database" = "app", "schema" = "doris_src",
    "include_tables" = "docs",
    "offset" = "initial"
)
TO DATABASE pg_mirror ("table.create.properties.replication_num" = "1");
```

## Changes arrive in seconds, schema changes included

The lab runs one Doris frontend and one backend next to pg16 and points a job at the project's
tables. On Doris 4.1.4 it found:

| | |
|---|---|
| source side | the job creates its own publication and slot, one per job, and `DROP JOB` removes both |
| latency | about 11 s with the default `max_interval` of 10, and about 5 s with 1 |
| types | `jsonb` lands as `text`, `uuid` as `text`, `timestamptz` as `datetime(6)` in the Doris time zone |
| `vector` | auto table creation refuses it, and in a pre-created table it arrives as NULL without an error |
| generated columns | copied by the snapshot, then dropped once streaming starts |
| DDL | added and dropped columns propagate |

Against [logical replication](logical-replication.qmd), the trade is latency for convenience.
Changes arrive in seconds instead of milliseconds, and schema changes come across on their own where
Postgres to Postgres stops the stream.

## Vectors arrive as NULL

Doris's CDC client is Debezium's Postgres connector, which has no converter for pgvector's `vector`
type, so the column arrives as NULL instead of failing. The workaround the notebook verifies is a
trigger on the source that keeps a `real[]` copy of each embedding. That copy arrives as
`ARRAY<FLOAT>`, and Doris's own `cosine_distance` then returns the same top five as pgvector.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sized for a server

The images are large (4 GB for the frontend, 9 GB for the backend), and their defaults assume a
dedicated machine, with an 8 GB heap and a backend sized to 90% of memory. On Docker Desktop that ends
in `MEM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The lab's compose file caps both (`DORIS_FE_HEAP`, `DORIS_BE_MEM`) so they
fit beside the other containers.
:::

::: {.chapter-notebook}
The measurements come from the [Doris CDC notebook](../notebooks/doris_cdc.ipynb), run against
servers started with `just db doris`.
:::
